# Data Preparation and Cleaning

## This quarto file performs the following actions:

**Imports files:**

- Imports full data set("artists_complete.csv") and stores it as artists_raw
- Imports data dictionary("artists_data_dictionary.csv) and stores it as artists_dictionary

**Checks for missing values**

**Cleans artists_raw**

- Creates artists_clean (copy of artists_raw)
- Replaces special codes 77(don't know) and 98(no response) with NA

**Converts some variables to ordered categorical variables**

- INCOME (household income)
- EDUC_R (highest education attained)

**Creates searchable variable catalog**

- by keyword
- by question number

**Creates 5 smaller data frames, retaining full data set artists_cleaned**

- artists_q1 (artistic disciplines respondents practice)
- artists_q2 (how respondents participate in these disciplines, including hobbyist, teachers, etc.)
- artists_q3 (additional information about respondents' artistic disciplines)
- artists_q58 (unpaid, volunteer and cultural activities across discipline)
- artists_q68 (employment benefits and which jobs provide them)
- artists_core (everything else)

## How to search data dictionary:

For example, to find all variables related to "income", use:

- artists_dictionary %\>% filter(str_detect(description, regex("income", ignore_case=TRUE)))

## How to use searchable variable catalog

For example to find "employment", use:

- find_vars("employment")

## Importing libraries and data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
```

```{r}
#import full data set
artists_raw <- read_csv("artists_complete.csv",
                        na = c("", " ", "NA"),
                        #don't display column types
                        show_col_types=FALSE)

#import data dictionary
artists_dictionary <- read_csv("artists_data_dictionary.csv")
```

## Checking for missing values

```{r}
#checking for missing values
artists_raw %>%
  summarise(total_missing = sum(is.na(across(everything()))))
```

```{r}
#examining missing values by variable
artists_raw %>% 
  #calculating percentage of missing values
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ mean(is.na(.x)) * 100)) %>% 
  #creating table showing percentages of missing values in each column
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "percent_missing") %>% 
  #arranging high to lowest percentages
  arrange(desc(percent_missing))
```

## Cleaning artists_raw

```{r}
#creating copy of artists_raw and organize columns
artists_clean <- artists_raw %>% 
  #changing order of columns to move ID, WEIGHTS, VSTRAT, and VPSU to the beginning
  relocate(ID, WEIGHTS, VSTRAT, VPSU)
```

```{r}
#investigating which variables contain codes 77 (don't know) and 98 (no response) as responses and looking at corresponding descriptions:
special_codes <- artists_clean %>% 
  #looking for 77 or 98 as a response
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), ~ sum(.x %in% c(77, 98), na.rm=TRUE))) %>% 
  #creating table with results
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "count") %>% 
  #removing variables without codes 77 and 98
  filter(count>0) %>% 
  #matching variable to dictionary alongside count
  left_join(artists_dictionary, by = "variable")
```

```{r}
#replacing special codes with NA
artists_clean <- artists_clean %>% 
  mutate(across(all_of(missing_vars), ~ replace(.x, .x %in% c(77, 98), NA_real_)))

#checking
tibble(dataset = c("Original", "Cleaned"), missing_values = c(sum(is.na(artists_raw)), sum(is.na(artists_clean))))
```

## Converting categorical variables to ordered categorical variables

```{r}
#organizing categorical variables, converting INCOME (household income) to ordered cat var
artists_clean <- artists_clean %>% 
  mutate(INCOME=factor(INCOME, levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4), labels = c("Under $30,000", "$30,000-$59,999", "$60,000-$99,999", "$100,000 or more"), ordered=TRUE))

#converting EDUC_R (highest educational attainment) to ordered cat var
artists_clean <- artists_clean %>% 
  mutate(EDUC_R=factor(EDUC_R, levels = c(1, 2, 3, 4), labels = c("High school or less", "Some college / Associate degree", "Bachelor's degree", "Graduate / Professional degree"), ordered=TRUE))

```

## Creating searchable variable catalog

```{r}
#creating searchable variable catalog
find_vars <- function(keyword) {artists_dictionary %>% 
    filter(str_detect(description, regex(keyword, ignore_case=TRUE))) %>% 
    select(variable, description)}
```

```{r}
#count variables by question
question_groups <- artists_dictionary %>% 
  mutate(question = str_extract(variable, "^Q[0-9]+")) %>% 
  count(question, sort=TRUE)

print(question_groups, n= 20)
```

```{r}
#adding question groups to dictionary
artists_dictionary <- artists_dictionary %>% 
  mutate(question = str_extract(variable, "^Q[0-9]+"))
```

```{r}
#To use: for example, to see all Q2 vars:
artists_dictionary %>% 
  filter(question == "Q2") %>% 
  select(variable, description)
```

## Creating smaller sub data sets

```{r}
#creating smaller data sets from artists_clean

#starting with Q2:
artists_q2 <- artists_clean %>% 
  select(ID, matches("^Q2([^0-9]|$)"))

#checking
dim(artists_q2)
```

```{r}
#creating smaller data sets for Q1, Q3 and Q58

#function to extract question group
get_question <- function(q){artists_clean %>% 
    select(ID, all_of(artists_dictionary %>% 
                        filter(question == q) %>% 
                        pull(variable)))}

```

```{r}
#creating sub data sets
artists_q1 <- get_question("Q1")
artists_q3 <- get_question("Q3")
artists_q58 <- get_question("Q58")

#checking sizes
sapply(list(artists_q1, artists_q3, artists_q58), dim)
```

```{r}
#creating artists_core, smaller dataframe minus questions 1, 2, 3 and 58

#excluding questions above
artists_core <- artists_clean %>% 
  select(-matches("Q(1|2|3|58)([^0-9]|$)"))

#checking
dim(artists_core)
```

```{r}
#looking for other large variable questions
artists_dictionary %>% 
  filter(variable %in% names(artists_core)) %>% 
  count(question, sort=TRUE)
```

```{r}
#separating out question 68:
artists_q68 <- get_question("Q68")

#removing from artists_core
artists_core <- artists_core %>% 
  select(-matches("^Q68([^0-9]|$)"))
```

```{r}
#checking
dim(artists_q68)
dim(artists_core)
```
